title: Key won't turn in the ignition
h1: Why won't my key turn in the ignition?
metaDesc: Key won't turn and the steering wheel is locked? Answer a few quick questions to free it safely, spot a worn key or lock, and know when to call a locksmith.
synonyms: steering wheel locked and key won't turn
key won't come out of ignition
intro: A key that won't turn is usually the steering lock holding the ignition, not a broken car. Most of the time you can free it in seconds with the right technique. If that doesn't work, the clues below separate a worn key from a worn lock so you know who to call.
safety: Never turn the key to Lock or pull it out while the car is moving. The steering can lock.
If the engine has ever shut off when the key was bumped or the key ring swung while driving, don't drive it until the ignition switch is checked.

q_wheel.help: Most cars lock the steering wheel when the key is out. If the wheel was turned when you parked, the lock pushes on the ignition and stops the key from turning.

opts.a: The steering wheel is locked and only moves a tiny bit either way
The steering wheel turns freely, but the key won't
The key won't go into the slot all the way
The key won't turn back to Off, or it won't come out

q_wiggle.q: Gently rock the steering wheel left and right while you turn the key. What happens?
q_wiggle.help: Use light, steady pressure on the key, and push the wheel toward the side that has a little give. Don't force the key or use tools on it.

opts.a: The key turned and the wheel unlocked
It still won't turn, no matter which way I rock the wheel

q_spare.q: Have you tried a spare key?
q_spare.help: A spare that has hardly been used is the fastest way to tell a worn key from a worn lock.

opts.a: Yes, and the spare turns normally
Yes, and the spare won't turn either
I don't have one, or haven't tried it
The key has felt sticky or needed jiggling for weeks
My key is visibly worn, bent, or a new copy
It worked fine, then suddenly wouldn't turn at all

result.title: It was likely the steering lock holding the key
result.now: If the key now turns smoothly every time, this was most likely the steering lock under pressure. Next time, straighten the wheels before you shut the car off and avoid leaning on the wheel as you get out.
if: If you need to rock the wheel almost every time, or it's getting harder, have the ignition lock checked before it jams for good.
If the car then won't crank or start, see our guide for when the car won't start.
result.why: The steering lock is a pin that drops into the steering column when the key is out. If the wheel is turned against it, the pin is pinched so tightly that the key can't turn. Rocking the wheel takes the pressure off and lets the key turn.

causes.name: Steering lock under tension
causes.clues: The wheel was turned when you parked, you parked against a curb, or the wheel got bumped after the key came out.

causes.name: Early wear in the ignition lock
causes.clues: It takes more force than it used to, even with the wheel straight.
causes.against: If it only happens after parking with the wheels turned, wear is less likely.

you: Park with the wheels straight and see if the problem goes away.
Notice whether the key turns easily when there's no pressure on the wheel.

result.title: Your key may be worn down or cut slightly wrong
result.now: Use the spare key if you have one, and have a new key made from the original factory code or the spare, not copied from the worn key.
if: If no key will turn, the lock itself is the more likely problem. Call a locksmith or the dealer.
If your car has a chip in the key, the new key will also need to be programmed to the car, or it may turn but not start.
result.why: The small cuts on a key wear down over years of use. Once they're rounded off, the pins inside the lock don't line up and the key won't turn. A copy made from a worn key copies the wear too.

causes.name: Worn key
causes.clues: The edges look smooth and rounded, the key is years old, or it works better when you wiggle it.
causes.against: If the spare won't turn either, the key isn't the main problem.

causes.name: Poorly cut copy
causes.clues: The problem started with a newly made key.

causes.name: Bent key
causes.clues: The key isn't straight when you sight down it, or a heavy key ring hangs from it.

you: Compare the main key and the spare side by side for rounded cuts.
Lighten a heavy key ring. The weight wears the lock and the key over time.
shop: Key programming if the key has a chip

result.title: The ignition lock may be wearing out
result.now: Book a locksmith or shop to look at the ignition lock soon, before it leaves you stuck somewhere. Until then, turn the key gently and don't force it.
if: If it gets to the point where only lots of jiggling works, treat it as urgent. It can jam completely at any time.
If the engine ever shuts off when the key is bumped while driving, don't drive it until it's repaired.
result.why: The ignition lock has small spring-loaded pins that wear along with the key. When it gradually gets harder to turn over weeks, lock wear is a common reason, and it rarely fixes itself.

causes.name: Worn ignition lock cylinder
causes.clues: It's gotten slowly worse, and the spare key is no better.

causes.name: Dirt or a dried-up lock
causes.clues: It's worse in cold or dusty conditions.

causes.name: Worn key
causes.clues: A spare key turns more easily.
causes.against: If the spare is just as stiff, the lock is the more likely culprit.

you: Try the spare key and compare how it feels.
Note whether a heavy key ring hangs from the key while driving.
shop: Lock cylinder repair or replacement, keyed to your existing key, if it is worn

result.title: The ignition lock may have jammed
result.now: Stop trying to force it. Call a locksmith who works on cars, or have the car towed to a shop or dealer.
if: If the lock looks scratched, pried or damaged, someone may have tried to steal the car. Take photos and consider reporting it.
If the key snaps off in the lock, leave the broken piece and call a locksmith.
result.why: When a key that worked fine suddenly won't turn, even with the wheel loose, something inside the lock may have broken or seized. Forcing it risks snapping the key or damaging the steering column.

causes.name: Failed ignition lock cylinder
causes.clues: A sudden change with no warning, and no key works.

causes.name: Damage from a theft attempt
causes.clues: Scratches or pry marks around the lock, or a loose trim cover.

causes.name: Steering lock stuck
causes.clues: The wheel is also locked solid and doesn't move at all.
causes.against: If the wheel turns freely, the steering lock isn't the problem.

you: Make sure you're using the right key for this car.
Look around the lock for scratches or pry marks.
shop: Ignition lock cylinder inspection, and repair or replacement if it has failed

result.title: Something is blocking the key, or the key is damaged
result.now: Check that you have the right key and that it's clean and straight, then look into the slot with a flashlight for dirt or a foreign object.
if: If the spare key goes in fine, have a new key cut from the spare or by code, not copied from the damaged one.
If no key will go in, or the lock looks damaged, call a locksmith rather than forcing it.
result.why: If the key won't slide in all the way, the pins in the lock can't line up, so it will never turn. That's often something on the key or in the slot, not a problem deeper in the car.

causes.name: Dirty, bent or damaged key
causes.clues: Gunk on the key, a visible bend, or a chipped edge.

causes.name: Debris or a foreign object in the lock
causes.clues: You can see something in the slot, or a child may have pushed something in.

causes.name: Damaged lock
causes.clues: Scratches, pry marks or a loose face on the lock.

you: Wipe the key clean and check that it's straight.
Shine a light into the slot.

result.title: The car may not register that it's in Park
result.now: With your foot on the brake, move the shifter firmly all the way into Park, then try turning the key back to Off.
if: If it still won't release and the dash lights are dim or dark, a weak battery may be the cause, since many cars need power to release the key.
If it happens often, have the shifter linkage and the key release checked.
If the car moved or rolled when you thought it was in Park, set the parking brake firmly before getting out and have the shifter checked before relying on Park again.
result.why: Automatic cars won't let the key turn to Lock or come out unless the transmission is fully in Park. If the shifter is a hair short of Park, or the part that senses Park is out of adjustment, the key stays trapped.

causes.name: Shifter not fully in Park
causes.clues: Moving the shifter or rocking the car slightly lets the key out.

causes.name: Weak or dead battery
causes.clues: Dim dash lights, or the car was slow to start.

causes.name: Faulty key release or shifter linkage
causes.clues: It keeps happening even when the shifter is firmly in Park.

you: Push the shifter firmly into Park with your foot on the brake.
Check whether the dash lights come on brightly.

result.title: Try the simple fixes first, then call a locksmith
result.now: Make sure the car is in Park, then turn the key gently while rocking the steering wheel left and right. Try the spare key if you have one.
if: If nothing works, call a locksmith who works on cars, or roadside assistance.
If you see damage around the lock, don't force it, and consider whether someone tried to steal the car.
result.why: Most stuck keys come down to the steering lock, a worn key or a worn lock. The two quick checks above help rule out the most common causes before you pay for help.

causes.name: Steering lock under tension
causes.clues: The wheel feels locked.

causes.name: Worn key
causes.clues: A spare key works better.

causes.name: Worn or jammed ignition lock
causes.clues: No key works, even with the wheel loose.

you: Rock the wheel while turning the key.
